label: Moral cognition
blurb: How do people attribute blame and responsibility, and how do character and intentionality information shape those judgments?

label: Cross-cultural moral psychology
blurb: How do moral experiences and concepts vary across societies, and how can we build instruments that capture that variation?

label: The dynamics of consciousness
blurb: What mind-wandering is, whether attention can drift on purpose, and how the stream of thought moves between focus, fixation, and free flight.

label: Self-regulation, vigilance & cognitive control
blurb: The psychological and neurobiological basis of complex, temporally-extended action over time.

label: Memory & forgetting
blurb: The cognitive and neural basis of remembering, forgetting, and imagining alternatives, from prospective memory and episodic counterfactuals to how forgiveness reshapes the memory of being wronged.

label: Political psychology
blurb: Why do political opponents dislike each other so much, and how can we use the tools of the cognitive and social sciences to address this?
